identity.title: Legal Practicum
identity.byline: John Sonsteng and Damien Riehl, with Abby Breit, Editor

hero.eyebrow: A LIVING CASEBOOK · 50 YEARS OF METHOD
hero.heading: The Legal Practice Practicum: a working law firm simulation for law students and lawyers to learn, develop, and enhance law practice and law management skills. Practice ready.

lede.p1: The Legal Practicum System is an innovative teaching and learning tool for law students and lawyers. The Practicum System is designed for lawyers at any level.
lede.p2: Try an experiment. Take a risk. Receive immediate feedback. Try again. Any time. No waiting in line. No coffee breaks. 24/7. A classroom of one. It is yours whenever you want.

hero.adopter_link: Law school, legal aid, or law firm? Use the practicum on your own cases

intro.skills_heading: The law practice and law practice management skills

after_skills.p1: For more than 50 years, a group of exceptional people — law students, law teachers, lawyers from firms large and small, judges, and non-lawyers — have worked together to develop the Legal Practicum System to assist law students and lawyers to learn, build, enhance, experiment, test ideas, strategy, and techniques, and take risks without fear of negative consequences.
after_skills.p2: Emerging technologies will help lawyers at all levels provide legal services quickly and at appropriate cost. Justice for all.
after_skills.p3: The Legal Practicum System is an open resource tool for all lawyers and law students at no cost. It may be edited and used to develop, learn, enhance, and perfect legal practice and legal management skills.
after_skills.p4: The Legal Practicum System is available to law students and lawyers throughout their careers, at any time, and is adaptable to any jurisdiction.

sonsteng.name: John Sonsteng
sonsteng.bio: John Sonsteng is an emeritus professor at Mitchell Hamline School of Law. He was a trial lawyer before he became a teacher. John has written many books and articles about advocacy. He is a Fulbright scholar and has taught effective advocacy skills throughout the United States and in many other countries.

riehl.name: Damien Riehl
riehl.bio: Damien Riehl is a lawyer-technologist with deep experience in litigation, cybersecurity, and AI. Admitted in 2002 and coding since 1985, he clerked for chief judges, litigated complex cases, and led global digital forensics teams. He now builds AI-driven legal systems. He co-chairs Minnesota's Connected and Automated Vehicles Council and chairs the MSBA AI Committee, advancing access-to-justice initiatives. He helped develop SALI's 18,000+ legal data standards and contributes to FOLIO's legal ontology. At Clio, he integrates AI into large-scale legal datasets. He also engages AI ethics work with global Catholic leaders and created the "All the Music" public-domain project.

M1.title: Foundational
M1.thesis: The groundwork — how to think, read, and carry yourself as a lawyer before the substance arrives.

M2.title: Substantive + Skills
M2.thesis: The trades of lawyering, learned on real-shaped matters across ten practice areas.

M3.title: Transition to Practice
M3.thesis: The business of law and the professional judgment that turns a graduate into a practitioner.

sample.title: Watch a sample consultation ▸
sample.description:
A recorded client interview — Devon Halvard, charged with DWI —
      played back turn by turn, then assessed with feedback. See the consultation room and the debrief in action
      before you bring your own key. Scripted sample, not a live AI client.

matters.description:
Ten practice shapes, each in the fictional State of Meridian
      and again in a real jurisdiction. Full packets, case files, rubrics, and interviews.

firm.title: Firm dashboard
firm.description:
Ellingboe & Ravndal LLP — the two-lawyer practicum firm.
      Fees, realization, AR aging, trust accounting, and budget, charted and taught.

templates.title: Deliverable templates
templates.description:
The six recurring course handouts — time sheet, engagement
      letter, interview plan, settlement plan, portfolio, and reflective report — each presented as a
      Planning Guide and Checklist with assessment and feedback notes. Print-ready.

centaur.title: People first; technology as the tool
centaur.description: Every exercise here ships with a machine-readable rubric and a revise-and-repeat loop. Faculty coach students through live work with people. Technology supplies more practice repetitions under faculty supervision. Technology gives the first-pass assessment and feedback, at any hour. The simulated client interviews, rubric feedback, and firm dashboard below support that practice.

getting_started.title: Getting started at your school
getting_started.description: Meet the people who run the practicum, shape it around your school, and find free matters and templates to begin.
